03-violin-plot-orchestra.visual_critic_note: Intentional Tol palette and clear typographic hierarchy elevate this above generic, but the shared y-scale causes Singapore and Mumbai violins to degenerate into unreadable horizontal needles, undermining the distribution encoding for 2 of 6 cities.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.encoding_integrity_note: Structurally honest: shared y-scale domain derived from d3.extent(allValues), violinScale domain from computed maxDensity, Silverman bandwidth is data-driven — only minor concern is the 0.5°C bandwidth floor that could over-smooth tight distributions and the small n=35 sample per cell making KDE marginal, but no zero-baseline violation (violin plots don't require one), no radius lie factor (linear density→width is correct for violins), and no dual-axis fabrication.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.stress_test_note: No update storms (pointermove only repositions tooltip), no transitions to interrupt, no cross-view dispatch loops, no stale scale closures (static render), and Pointer Events API unifies mouse/touch natively — interaction robustness is clean across all five criteria.
03-violin-plot-orchestra.cognitive_load_note: 72-cell split-violin grid stays readable because the two-color palette (blue/red) is perceptually clean, the shared y-scale turns all 72 cells into one conceptual unit, and seasonal structure (Oslo's dramatic swing vs Singapore's flat band) pops immediately — the only risk is cell size at smaller viewports where violin shapes would lose resolution.
